sentences.text: ( for short "SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act").
The Appellant is seeking regular bail.

The offences were registered under Sections 376(1)(d), 354-A,
354-C of Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC") and Sections 3(1)(w)(i) & (ii) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

Learned A.P.P. submitted that the provisions of the Atrocities Act are dropped on 12.11.2020 while filing the charge-sheet.

The application for bail was rejected by the learned Additional Sagar @ Shrikrishna Arjun Avghade vs State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80332835/

sentences.text: 1 Sessions Judge, Vaduj.
The application for bail was rejected after the filing of charge-sheet.

3. Since the appellant is not prosecuted for offences under Atrocities Act, the applicant is required for file application for regular bail in accordance with Section 434 of CrP.C. and not Appeal under Section 14-A of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
4. Leave to amend.
The appellant is permitted to convert the Appeal into the application for bail.
Amendment may be carried out within one week.
5. After the amendment is carried out, the matter be listed before the appropriate Court.
